member.name: T:SimulaSharp.CodeGen.ContainmentGenerator
member.summary: For every model decorated with [Contains<T>("Name")], emits the read-only containment accessor: a public Container<T> Name { get; init; } = Container<T>.Empty; per attribute. The accessor is init-only, so the generated simulator can fill it through an object initializer during assembly while a model can only enumerate it afterwards. The backing collection is built by the simulator via a ContainerFactory (see ); this generator only shapes the surface.

member.name: T:SimulaSharp.CodeGen.KnobGenerator
member.summary: For every partial model with knob-decorated partial properties, implements them (volatile get; volatile set + change-notify) and builds a Knob binder per knob via an explicit IKnobProvider.CollectKnobs the simulator calls during discovery. v1 covers value knobs (Text/TickBox/Number<T>) plus trigger knobs.

member.name: T:SimulaSharp.CodeGen.LocalReferenceGenerator
member.summary: For every model decorated with [Reference<T>("Name")] (an intra-site reference), emits the read-only list accessor and the hidden fill seam. Because the targets share this model's SimSite, there is no Ref wrapping and no marshalling: per attribute it emits a private readonly List<T> __local_Name and a public IReadOnlyList<T> Name => __local_Name; accessor (getters only). It implements ILocalReferenceWiring.WireLocalReference explicitly — the generated simulator calls it after construction with the target IModel instances themselves, which the seam casts to the reference's element type and appends. (Contrast , the cross-site variant over guarded Refs.)

member.name: T:SimulaSharp.CodeGen.ParameterGenerator
member.summary:
For every partial model/service with [Parameter]-marked members, emits two things into the partial:
an internal __ApplyParameters(IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string?>) that binds the assembly's (weakly-typed, textual) Config values into the strongly-typed members — when a key is present it is converted and assigned; when it is absent the attribute's default is applied (or, for a Required parameter, an error is thrown);
an explicit IParameterProvider.CollectParameters that builds one ParameterInfo binder per parameter (boxed read/write over the member), so the simulator can expose GetParams()/SetParam().
The generated simulator calls both while assembling (in its constructor), before Configure(). A parameter may also carry [Knob]/[Plottable]; this generator only references the member, so it composes with the field the knob generator materializes.

member.name: T:SimulaSharp.CodeGen.PlottableGenerator
member.summary:
For every partial model with [Plottable] properties, implements IPlottableProvider.CollectPlottables — building a Plottable binder per member whose Sample delegate does a volatile read (through the member's volatile getter) projected to double.
Materialization is coordinated with : a plottable property that is also a knob is already materialized (volatile backing field + partial get/set) by the knob generator, so here we only reference it. A plottable-only partial property is materialized here (volatile get + set, no change-notify — plottable is observe-only). Either way the sampler reads the same volatile getter.

member.name: T:SimulaSharp.CodeGen.ReferenceGenerator
member.summary: For every model decorated with [References<T>("Name")], emits the read-only reference accessor and the hidden fill seam. Per attribute it emits a readonly IReference<{T}Ref> __ref_Name backed by a FillableReference<{T}Ref> and a public IReference<{T}Ref> Name => __ref_Name; accessor (getters only — no Add on the model's surface). It also implements IReferenceWiring.WireReference explicitly: the generated simulator calls it with a RefCollection of pre-wrapped target Refs, which the seam downcasts to the reference's Ref type (valid because a referenced model's Ref implements the companion interface — see ) and appends to the fillable backing.

member.name: T:SimulaSharp.CodeGen.RefGenerator
member.summary:
Emits the guarded cross-site reference wrappers. For each interface I used as a [CrossReference<I>] target it emits a single sealed class <I>Ref : IModelRef that wraps an I target and the two schedulers captured at construction (the target's and the caller's), then routes each of I's members by a three-tier taxonomy:
[Triggerable] void methods → fire-and-forget: same-site inline, cross-site Post.
[VolatileAccess] get-only properties → a plain synchronous getter (=> _target.P), no dispatch.
everything else → async request/response: same-site inline + completed Task, cross-site InjectAsync/InjectVoidAsync.
Because a cross-reference target is always the interface, there is exactly one Ref per interface — no per-model Ref classes and no companion Ref interfaces (the target opacity makes them unnecessary).

member.name: T:SimulaSharp.CodeGen.ServiceGenerator
member.summary:
Emits the interaction plumbing for services (types implementing SimulaSharp.Kernel.Model.IService, declared partial):
For each [ServiceEvent("X", argType?)] — a fire-and-forget publish point — a backing ServiceEventChannel, a public RegisterCallback_X(dispatcher, callback) for subscribers (the subscriber passes its site's IDispatcher), and a protected Trigger_X(...) the service calls to publish (Posts each callback onto its subscriber's dispatcher). Returning events (a result type) are not yet generated.
For each [ServiceRequest] method Handle_X(..) — a public X(..) caller that marshals the call onto the service's own site (Site.Inject*, the common IDispatcher facet, so it works on both the sim-paced and loosely-coupled service bases) and returns an awaitable (Task/Task<T>).

member.name: T:SimulaSharp.CodeGen.SimulatorGenerator
member.summary:
Generates a <Name>Simulator : SimulatorBase from each *.simassembly.yaml (an AdditionalFiles item), parsed with YamlDotNet. The generated constructor creates the sites, constructs the services and the model tree (depth-first, wiring containment and applying parameters), binds service dependencies, discovers knobs/plottables/parameters, and calls OnAssembled — so a freshly-constructed simulator is already assembled and ready to tune then Configure.
Conventions (v1): YAML Type is the fully-qualified type name; models have a (IClock, IScheduler, ILogger) ctor and services a (IClock, ILogger) ctor; the generated class lives in the global namespace with a parameterless ctor.
